## Discovery & Translational Science

* **Neuro-chimeric human organoid mouse models developed for brain research** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/16/human-brain-organoids-neuro-chimeric-mice-study-published-nature/)
  * Researchers generated mice with half a brain and filled the remaining space with human brain organoids to construct neuro-chimeric models.
  * The strategy aims to open new research avenues for studying complex human neurological development and disease biology *in vivo*.

* **c-KIT identified as a ciliary receptor driving pancreatic alpha-cell proliferation** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.10.750659)
  * Proteomic profiling of primary cilia in pancreatic α-cells identified the receptor tyrosine kinase c-KIT as a novel ciliary receptor.
  * Stimulation with its endogenous ligand stem cell factor (SCF) required intact primary cilia to promote α-cell proliferation, providing a mechanistic link to hyperglucagonemia in diabetes.

* **Recurrent chromatin regulator mutations predict response to immune checkpoint therapy** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.15.26363151)
  * Pan-cancer analysis identified distinct sets of chromatin regulator (CR) gene mutations associated with improved overall survival following immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) treatment across 10 cancer types.
  * Co-occurrence of mutations in two or more CR genes correlated with higher tumor mutational burden and enhanced pro-survival outcomes post-ICI therapy.

* **Pathogenic MUC1-fs target characterized in ADTKD-MUC1 cell models** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.16.26363125)
  * Established immortalized primary tubular cell models from autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease (ADTKD-MUC1) patients to track the pathogenic frameshift neoprotein MUC1-fs.
  * MUC1-fs exhibited a significantly longer half-life than wild-type mucin 1; targeting the secretory pathway with small-molecule compound BRD4780 successfully downregulated MUC1-fs accumulation.

* **Lineage-restricted targeting drives shift of T-cell engagers to autoimmune indications** [Andrew Pannu on X](https://x.com/andrewpannu/status/2100228219555172387)
  * Analysis of over 750 T-cell engager (TCE) programs indicates a strategic transition from oncology to autoimmune diseases.
  * TCEs demonstrate optimal therapeutic windows when targeting clean, lineage-restricted cell populations (such as B-cell depletion), where lower toxicity thresholds are required compared to solid tumors.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **[Biotech]** **Skyhawk Therapeutics reports positive 15-month data for Huntington's candidate** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/skyhawk-huntingtons-drug-rna-splicing-results/830537/)
  * Final phase study results for SKY-0515, a once-daily oral RNA splicing modulator, demonstrated a 0.94-point improvement on a composite Huntington's disease functional scale at 15 months (a 1.59-point advantage over natural history controls).
  * High-dose treatment consistently lowered mutant huntingtin (mHTT) protein levels by >60% with no reported serious adverse events.
  * SKY-0515 is currently being evaluated across two larger clinical studies.

* **Canakinumab and emavusertib evaluated in lower-risk MDS phase 2 trials** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42749863/)
  * Results from the Phase 2 CANFIRE and LUCAS open-label trials assessed the efficacy of interleukin-1β inhibitor canakinumab and IRAK4 inhibitor emavusertib for treating anemia in patients with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS).

* **[Biotech]** **Sellas Life Sciences faces potential setback in AML trial** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/17/sellas-immunotherapy-study-acute-myeloid-leukemia/)
  * Sellas' clinical trial evaluating an experimental immunotherapy for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) faces severe delays and execution issues, raising concerns over trial outcome and program viability.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Big Pharma]** **Roche's Lunsumio meets primary endpoint in Phase 3 Celestimo trial** [Jacob Plieth on X](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2100518925733634542)
  * Roche announced that Lunsumio (mosunetuzumab) achieved a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) in the Phase 3 Celestimo trial for patients with follicular lymphoma.
  * Overall survival (OS) data remain immature at the time of analysis.

* **Readjudicated Phase 3 ADVOCATE trial confirms avacopan efficacy in ANCA-associated vasculitis** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.16.26363171)
  * A 2026 independent readjudication of the ADVOCATE trial verified primary outcomes, showing week-26 remission rates of 68.1% for avacopan vs. 67.1% for prednisone taper in granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) and microscopic polyangiitis (MPA).
  * Sustained remission at week 52 met predefined non-inferiority and superiority criteria, confirming previously published efficacy and safety parameters.

* **[Biotech]** **Sling Therapeutics secures $123M Series C for Phase 3 TED trial** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/sling-linsitinib-series-c-financing-thyroid-eye-disease/830452/)
  * Sling Therapeutics closed a $123 million Series C financing to advance linsitinib into late-stage Phase 3 clinical testing for thyroid eye disease (TED).
  * Linsitinib is an oral, twice-daily small molecule inhibitor of IGF-1R designed to offer a convenient alternative to infused or injected antibodies such as Tepezza (**[Big Pharma]** Amgen) and Lumvoa (**[Biotech]** Viridian).

## Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Biotech]** **Aquestive Therapeutics resubmits NDA for Anaphylm sublingual film** [BioStocks on X](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2100552016313340255)
  * Resubmitted its New Drug Application (NDA) to the FDA for Anaphylm, a polymer-based sublingual film formulation of epinephrine for treating Type I allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis.

* **FDA identifies new FAERS safety signals for Acthar Gel and Beyfortus** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/fda-adverse-event-monitoring-system-aems/january-march-2026-new-safety-information-or-potential-signals-serious-risks-identified-fda-adverse)
  * The FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS) flagged drug hypersensitivity for Acthar Gel (repository corticotropin) and immune thrombocytopenia for Beyfortus (**[Big Pharma]** nirsevimab-alip).
  * The FDA is evaluating post-market data to determine if label changes or regulatory actions are required.

* **FDA grants full traditional approval to Tecartus in mantle cell lymphoma** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/verified-clinical-benefit-cancer-accelerated-approvals)
  * The FDA converted the accelerated approval of Tecartus (**[Big Pharma]** brexucabtagene autoleucel) to full traditional approval for adult patients with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after confirmatory trial data verified clinical benefit.

* **FDA launches pilot program to expedite human trial starts** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/09/16/fda-plans-to-speed-approvals-experimental-drugs-in-montana/)
  * Opened applications for a pilot program intended to shorten regulatory review timelines for drug sponsors seeking clearance to begin Phase 1 first-in-human clinical testing.

* **FDA clarifies compounding restrictions as GLP-1 shortages ease** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-clarifies-policies-compounders-national-glp-1-supply-begins-stabilize)
  * Reminded 503A and 503B compounding pharmacies that producing drugs that are "essentially copies" of commercially available GLP-1 receptor agonists is prohibited as commercial drug supply stabilizes.

* **FDA CDER launches C3TI Compass knowledge repository** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/about-fda/cder-center-clinical-trial-innovation-c3ti/c3ti-compass-knowledge-repository)
  * Established the CDER Center for Clinical Trial Innovation (C3TI) Compass, a centralized database housing guidance documents, case studies, and tools supporting novel clinical trial designs and trial-to-real-world-data (RWD) linkages.

## Business & Strategy

* **[Big Pharma]** **Novartis acquires Sironax blood-brain barrier delivery platform for $125M** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/novartis-125m-for-blood-brain-barrier-crossing-platform-Sironax/830560/)
  * Novartis exercised its option to acquire full ownership of Sironax's drug delivery platform engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier for $125 million upfront.
  * Sironax will retain rights to continue clinical development of select internal assets derived from the platform.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Roche enters $1B bispecific antibody discovery deal with Dualitas** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/roche-dualitas-bispecific-antibodies-immune/830573/)
  * Roche partnered with Dualitas Therapeutics in a deal worth $36.5 million upfront plus up to $1 billion in development and commercial milestones.
  * Dualitas will leverage its high-throughput screening platform to evaluate over 300,000 bispecific antibody combinations targeting immune-mediated diseases, with Roche holding options to advance selected programs.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Novo Nordisk collaborates with Anthropic for AI-assisted R&D** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/novo-anthropic-ai-drug-discovery-development-deal/830540/)
  * Partnered with AI firm Anthropic to deploy frontier Claude models across target discovery, internal software engineering, and R&D workflows.

* **[Biotech]** **Tempest Therapeutics pivots pipeline toward in vivo CAR-T platforms** [Jacob Plieth on X](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2100219334765256717)
  * Tempest announced a strategic redirection focusing on *in vivo* CAR-T therapeutics, positioning its platform against similar approaches pursued by Gilead and Interius.

* **[Biotech]** **Hedge fund launches startup North Immunology for long-acting antibodies** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/17/biotech-hedge-fund-startup-north-immunology/)
  * A biotech hedge fund built and launched North Immunology from inception to engineer long-acting antibody therapeutics aimed at treating atopic dermatitis.

## Public Health & Policy

* **[Big Pharma]** **NICE to cover AstraZeneca’s Enhertu in England following US-UK trade dialogue** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/17/astrazeneca-enhertu-breast-cancer-england-nice-pricing-agreement-us-trade-deal/)
  * England’s National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) reached a reimbursement agreement to cover Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan) for HER2-positive breast cancer, influenced in part by US-UK drug pricing discussions.

* **Real-world data confirms maternal RSVpreF vaccine protection in infants** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.15.26363141)
  * A test-negative real-world study showed maternal RSVpreF (**[Big Pharma]** Pfizer) vaccine effectiveness was 73.9% against medically attended RSV infection and 86.3% against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants <6 months.
  * Initial protection matched long-acting monoclonal antibody nirsevimab (**[Big Pharma]** Sanofi/AstraZeneca), but maternal vaccine protection waned ~1.7 times faster.

* **Lawsuit alleges NIH violated First Amendment rights via keyword grant screening** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/16/lawsuit-argues-nih-violated-researcher-first-amendment-rights-aclu/)
  * The ACLU filed a lawsuit against the NIH, arguing that automated searching and filtering of grant applications for specific disfavored terms to trigger rejections violates applicants' First Amendment rights.

* **WHO notes progress in Democratic Republic of the Congo Ebola response** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/16/ebola-outbreak-drc-who-cautious-optimism/)
  * The World Health Organization expressed cautious optimism regarding containment efforts and epidemiological trends for the current Ebola virus outbreak in the DRC.

* **FDA hiring expansion hampered by centralized administrative bottlenecks** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/17/fda-doge-cuts-new-hires-slowed-centralized-hiring-center-short-staffed/)
  * Initiatives to onboard thousands of new technical and medical personnel across the FDA are being delayed by backlogs at an understaffed centralized human resources center.
